title: Longest common subsequence (2D DP)
summary: Fill a table where each cell is the answer for two shorter prefixes, building up to the whole strings.
note: A subsequence keeps the letters' order but can skip letters.

panels.label: dp[i][j]: longest common subsequence of a's first i and b's first j letters

marks.label: letters match
marks.when: row > 0 and col > 0 and a[row - 1] == b[col - 1]

narration.text: a has {m} letters and b has {n}.
Start with a table of zeros: an empty prefix has nothing in common with anything.
Row {i}: prefixes of a that end in {a[i - 1]}.
They match, so take the diagonal cell and add this letter.
They differ, so keep the better of dropping a letter from a or from b.
dp[{i}][{j}] is the larger of {dp[i - 1][j]} (above) and {dp[i][j - 1]} (left): {dp[i][j]}.
The longest common subsequence has {dp[m][n]} letters.
